title: Say not, I am a child (Jeremiah 1:4–10)
hookLine: the young prophet protests, and God touches his mouth
carry: it was never about your size
last: NOBODY'S HARVEST GOES TO SOMEONE ELSE.

lines: BEFORE I FORMED THEE, I KNEW THEE.
cards: The book of Jeremiah opens with a call, and the first thing the prophet does is say no. The word of the Lord comes to him: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee."
Before you were born, I set you apart and made you a prophet to the nations. Jeremiah's answer comes straight back. "Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child."
Wrong person, too young, no words. Moses, at the burning bush, made a similar case: I'm slow of speech.

teach.h: SAY NOT, I AM A CHILD.
teach.b: The answer begins with the two words that give us today's word. "Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak."
The Hebrew word Jeremiah uses for himself is na'ar: a boy, a youth, a young man. The text never tells us his age, and readers have guessed in different directions.
What the story cares about is how he sees himself: too small for this. Notice what God doesn't do. He doesn't argue that Jeremiah is older than he thinks, or more gifted, or more ready.
No flattery at all. The weight moves somewhere else: you'll go where I send you, and say what I give you. "Be not afraid of their faces: for I am with thee."

teach.h: I HAVE PUT MY WORDS IN THY MOUTH.
teach.b: The Lord puts out his hand and touches Jeremiah's mouth: "Behold, I have put my words in thy mouth." Jeremiah named his problem as his mouth, and that's exactly where the touch lands.
The call closes with a list of verbs: to root out and to pull down, to destroy and to throw down, to build and to plant. Most are about tearing down, and his book will have plenty of that.

But the list ends on building and planting. So say not, I am a child isn't a promise that he'll stop feeling small. It's permission to speak anyway, because the words were never supposed to come from his size.

how: Jeremiah's call is read in synagogue as a haftarah, the reading from the Prophets that follows the Torah reading, in the summer weeks before Tisha b'Av.

o: a warning to keep quiet until you're older
a rule that children may not speak in worship
God's answer: don't measure the call by your size

games.q: say not, I am a child — tap the pairs.

s: the text says Jeremiah was a young teenager
it never gives his age; he calls himself na'ar, a word for a boy or a youth.
God answers by touching Jeremiah's mouth
behold, I have put my words in thy mouth.
God tells Jeremiah he's more gifted than he thinks
there's no flattery: you'll go where I send you, and I am with thee.

games.q: you're Jeremiah. you've just told God you can't speak: you're only a youth. what comes back?
o: say not, I am a child: go, and speak.
wait a few years, then ask again.
games.why: God won't take the excuse, and then touches his mouth: behold, I have put my words in thy mouth.

practice: Bring to mind a room where you tend to go quiet, a meeting or a family table where everyone seems older or surer, and find the one thing you'd say there if size didn't matter: a question, a fact, a disagreement, a thank-you.
Say it once to yourself, plainly, in your head. If you pray, you can hold the words God said to Jeremiah: say not, I am a child.

wordCard.voice: Say not. God's answer to a prophet who called himself a child: the call isn't measured by your size. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: say not, I am a child (a youth), from Jeremiah 1:7.

carryVoice: Your line: it was never about your size. The touch landed right where he felt smallest. See you tomorrow.
